items.title: El Niño effect: Andhra declares 388 mandals drought-hit; 283 face severe conditions
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has declared drought in 388 of the state’s 688 mandals across 21 districts for the 2026 kharif season. The government has declared 283 mandals as severely drought-affected and 105 as moderately affected. The Revenue (Disaster Management) Department issued a government order on October 1, following recommendations by the State Drought Committee, which met on September 30 to assess drought conditions. The government opted for an early declaration instead of waiting until the October 31 deadline, citing a significant rainfall deficit and prevailing El Niño conditions. Andhra Pradesh recorded an average rainfall of 197.6 mm between June 1 and August 31, against the normal of 424.3 mm, marking a deficit of 53.4%, according to the government order. The assessment was conducted in accordance with the Government of India's Manual for Drought Management, 2016. The drought declaration covers Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam, Markapuram, Kurnool, Nandyal, Ananthapuramu, Sri Sathya Sai, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya and Chittoor districts. Her death has raised questions about the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, with her family alleging foul play and demanding a thorough investigation. Himashri, a student of B Borooah College in Guwahati, had travelled to Andhra Pradesh with a dance troupe to participate in cultural programmes. During the journey, Himashri allegedly contacted her friends and family members, saying she felt unsafe in a coach occupied by a group of men. Her family said she also shared a video of the crowded compartment with a friend and spoke about being uncomfortable with the behaviour of some passengers. items.title: A ‘one-man’ Election Commission? Inside the allegations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: On October 6, around 240 Opposition MPs marched towards the Election Commission of India’s office in New Delhi, demanding a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and seeking his resignation. They were stopped a few hundred metres from the Commission’s office and eventually sat in protest. The Election Commission, however, gave a different account. In a press note issued that evening, it said it learnt through the media that MPs wanted to meet the Commission and that, until 4 pm, no political party representative had sought an appointment. Later, Delhi Police informed the Commission that a delegation led by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi wanted to submit a memorandum. The ECI said the delegation wanted to meet at Parliament House Annexe, whereas its protocol required such meetings to be held at the Commission’s premises. It offered to send a senior-most officer to receive the memorandum, but the MPs declined. The explanation may address the question of procedure. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday said that it will hear the case concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal on October 16. Pertinently, the Court on that date will consider whether voters excluded during the SIR process and who have filed appeals against the exclusion, should be allowed to vote for the upcoming municipal elections in the State. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana advanced the hearing amid concerns that voters whose appeals against exclusion from the electoral rolls remain pending may miss the November municipal elections. The Court also discussed prioritising appeals seeking inclusion in the electoral rolls over those seeking deletion of voters. "There are two priorities we are contemplating. One is that appeals filed by persons seeking deletion of voters can be pushed back and taken up at the last stage," said CJI Kant.
